answer: Picture identities as boats needing a berth: the network runs a fixed-supply harbor where every agent must win and continuously hold a scarce mooring slot, priced by open auction. One honest agent buys a single berth cheaply, but a sybil fleet must bid against itself for many slots at once, so each extra fake identity pays a steeper price - cost climbs superlinearly, like hauling sand up a dune. Flagged by peer audit, you forfeit the deposit, and your island of fakes drowns rather than anchors.
